So forward reaction: reactants: ClCH2Cl (dichloromethane) and a heterocycle (maybe a fluorinated piperidine fused to aromatic). Product: same heterocycle but with a chloromethyl substituent on aromatic ring (position 9). So retrosynthetic template would break that C-CH2Cl bond, giving precursors: the heterocycle (same as product but without CH2Cl) and CH2ClCl? Actually the template likely corresponds to substitution of a chloromethyl group onto aromatic ring via SN2? The product includes a CH2Cl attached to aromatic carbon (c:9). The precursor would be the same heterocycle with a hydrogen at that position (c:9) and CH2ClCl (or maybe CH2ClCl as reagent). In retrosynthesis, we would generate two precursors: the core scaffold (product without CH2Cl) and CH2ClCl (or maybe CH2ClCl is the reagent). The template ID 1914394 likely expects two precursors: the core and CH2ClCl.
